prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow path sloping downward and away from the high-mounted camera, lined left, right, and below by dense rosette shrubs whose nearest leaves at the bottom edge are brightest and within arm's reach (~0.5–1.5 m), while distant shrubs fade into dark grey (~3–6+ m). In front of the camera wearer along the central-right trail is a person with a pink backpack at roughly 2–2.5 m in frames 1–3, and slightly ahead and to their left (~0.5–1 m further away, ~2.5–3.5 m from the camera) is a second person in a dark poncho who is out of view in frame 1, partly cut off at the top in frames 2–4, and fully visible in frame 5. Both people face away from the camera wearer and are within arm's reach of each other by frames 4–5 as the camera wearer approaches and tilts upward, bringing the nearer person to roughly 1.2–1.5 m (just outside or at the edge of the camera wearer's reach) and the second person to ~2 m. Compared to the cluttered RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the foreground foliage tufts and the receding depth layering between the two hikers and the trail depression. However, the map is unreliable where it merges each person's backpack, poncho, and body into single smooth depth blobs, blurs thin spiky leaves into surrounding vegetation, and flattens the distant hillside and sky in frame 5 to uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground person in the pink backpack (light pink mask) in the upper-center to right across all five frames (~2–2.5 m away in frames 1–3, closing to ~1.2–1.5 m in frame 5) and the second person in the dark poncho (brownish-orange mask) directly ahead and to the first person's left in frames 4 and 5 (~2–3 m from the camera and within arm's reach, <1 m, of the first person). In frames 1–4 both people have their heads cropped by the top border and the nearer person's right side overlaps and partially occludes the further person, whereas in frame 5 the camera tilts up and steps closer so both full silhouettes appear lower in the frame facing away from the camera wearer. While the RGB strip shows their carried gear (pink backpack, purple bottle in the right pocket, black poncho) and the surrounding rosette plants within arm's reach (~0.5–1.5 m below the camera), the segmentation map makes the exact occlusion boundary between the two overlapping hikers in frames 4–5 immediately distinct. The map is unreliable in frames 2 and 3 where it completely fails to detect the partially visible person in the black poncho ahead on the left. Additionally, it merges worn backpacks and ponchos into the `person` masks without separate object labels and leaves all surrounding vegetation, trail surfaces, and the raised object in frame 5 unsegmented in black.
descriptions.pose: Across frames 1 to 4, the pose map is completely blank (all black), providing no spatial information about the two hikers walking 2–3.5 m ahead on the trail or the camera wearer. In frame 5, as the camera wearer approaches to within ~1.2–2 m and tilts upward, a single yellow body skeleton appears in the upper-center corresponding to the upper body of the person in the pink backpack (~1.2–1.5 m away) and/or the adjacent raised left arm of the person in the black poncho (~2 m away, immediately to the left and within arm's reach of the first person). The skeleton shows a raised limb extending upward toward the top edge where the poncho wearer's hand holds an object at arm's reach above head level, alongside a compact cluster of torso/head keypoints below and to the right, while both people face away from the camera wearer. Unlike the RGB image, which clearly shows two distinct people walking away, the pose map only highlights the elevated arm extension in frame 5 and fails to render any magenta hand skeletons. The map is highly unreliable throughout the sequence, missing both people entirely in frames 1–4 (when their heads are cropped at the top border and bodies are seen from behind under bulky gear) and producing a single distorted, incomplete upper-body skeleton in frame 5 that conflates keypoints between the two overlapping hikers and omits their legs.
